name: Dusky Purplish Grey
lede: Dusky Purplish Grey is a dark, near-neutral grey, built by stacking the modifiers dusky and purplish onto the base color grey rather than naming anything in particular.

sections.title: Two modifiers on grey
sections.body:
Dusky Purplish Grey stacks two modifier words, dusky and purplish, onto the base color [[grey]], in the compound-modifier grammar ColorHub's library uses for names like this one rather than a borrowed object or place [1]. Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* carries it as plate LIII, hue 67'''', an aged plate scan read as approximate [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 filed the same swatch under block 229, though by measurement it sits nearer block 151, dark grayish green [1]. In Munsell terms it reads as N 2.8, close to a true neutral with almost no hue of its own, which is why the "purplish" in its name barely shows on screen [1].

Its nearest named neighbors are [[blackish-slate]], 2.9 units off, and [[charcoal-grey]], 3.0 off [1], both close enough on screen to pass for the same dark ink.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a color within six units of this swatch in 632 of 23,781 paintings, 2.66 percent, as photographed; looking inside each painting for at least five percent coverage narrows that to 361 [2]. That makes it more common than 79 percent of the named colors in our library [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, present in 3.8 percent of our 1,674 paintings from that decade, 2.2 times the museums' baseline rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a mid-tone, in 42 percent of its 361 appearances by lightness rank [2].

André Derain is its most devoted painter on file, present in 5 of his 22 works here, several times the baseline rate for the museums that hold them [2]. The earliest match dates to 1099, eight centuries before the name's 1912 record, so it marks a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a surviving pigment [2]. It is most over-represented in paintings from the United Kingdom, and shares canvases with [[deep-neutral-grey|Deep Neutral Grey]] and [[moss-grey|Moss Grey]] more often than chance [2].
